comment:
<comment datatype="string">Citrate lyase is an anaerobic enzyme that catalyzes the cleavage of <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=CIT">citrate</a> to <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ACET">acetate</a> and <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=OXALACETIC_ACID">oxaloacetate</a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/6354265">Nilekani83</a>] (see <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=PWY-6038">citrate degradation</a>). Because the citrate molecule is very stable, it has to be activated by forming a thioester bond with the enzyme before cleavage can take place.
<p>
The enzyme is a complex of three subunits (in a 6:6:6 configuration), one of them a dedicated acyl carrier protein (acp).
The acp protein is synthesized in an <i>apo</i> form, and is converted to its <i>holo</i> form by the covalent binding of the prosthetic group <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=2-5-PHOSPHORIBOSYL-3-DEPHOSPHO-COA" title="<a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=2-5-PHOSPHORIBOSYL-3-DEPHOSPHO-COA''>2'-(5''-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA</a> is a cofactor of the enzymes <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=ACECITLY-CPLX''>citrate lyase</a> and <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CPLX-7660''>malonate decarboxylase complex</a>. The cofactor is attached via phosphodiester linkage to a serine residue of an acyl-carrier protein subunit of the enzyme complex.&#10;&#10;For biosynthesis of this cofactor, see <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=P2-PWY''>citrate lyase activation</a> and <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=PWY-5796''>malonate decarboxylase activation</a>.">2'-(5''-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA</a> to a serine residue. This prosthetic group is very unusual and the only other enzyme known to use it is <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CPLX-7660">malonate decarboxylase</a>.
<p>
The synthesis and attachment of the prosthetic group are catalyzed by two different enzymes. The first step, catalyzed by <a href="NEW-IMAGE?type=EC-NUMBER&object=EC-2.4.2.52">EC 2.4.2.52, triphosphoribosyl-dephospho-CoA synthase</a> is the formation of an unusual &alpha;-1,2-glycosidic linkage between ATP and dephospho-CoA, forming the prosthetic group and releaing adenine [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/10924139">Schneider00</a>]. In the second step, catalyzed by <a href="NEW-IMAGE?type=EC-NUMBER&object=EC-2.7.7.61">EC 2.7.7.61, citrate lyase holo-[acyl-carrier protein] synthase</a>, the group is transferred to the <i>apo</i>-[acp] protein, generating the <i>holo</i>-[acp] form [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11948157">Schneider02</a>].
<p>
The <i>holo</i> form is still not active - in order to be fully active, the prosthetic group needs to be acetylated. The most common enzyme performing the acetylation is <a href="NEW-IMAGE?type=EC-NUMBER&object=EC-6.2.1.22">EC 6.2.1.22, [citrate (<em>pro</em>-3<em>S</em>)-lyase] ligase</a>, which uses <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ACET">acetate</a> as the donor [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/4365579">Schmellenkamp74</a>]. A different enzyme, <a href="NEW-IMAGE?type=EC-NUMBER&object=EC-2.3.1.49">EC 2.3.1.49, deacetyl-[citrate-(<em>pro</em>-3<em>S</em>)-lyase] <em>S</em>-acetyltransferase</a>, that uses <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=S-ACETYLPHOSPHOPANTETHEINE">S-acetyl phosphopantetheine</a> as the acetyl donor, has been characterized from the bacterium <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-548"><i>Klebsiella aerogenes</i></a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/4741546">Singh73</a>].
<p>
Another enzyme that modulates the activity of <a href="NEW-IMAGE?type=EC-NUMBER&object=EC-4.1.3.6">citrate lyase</a> has been reported in the bacterium <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-28068"><i>Rubrivivax gelatinosus</i></a>. That enzyme, <a href="NEW-IMAGE?type=EC-NUMBER&object=EC-3.1.2.16">EC 3.1.2.16, citrate-lyase deacetylase</a>, converts the active acetyl form back into the inactive thiol form by removal of its acetyl groups [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7460909">Giffhorn80</a>].</comment>

<comment datatype="string">The <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=G-14821">citC</a> gene of <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-573"><i>Klebsiella pneumoniae</i></a> was discovered in an operon that also contained the three genes that encode the <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CPLX-8398">citrate lyase complex</a> complex and the <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=REACTION&object=2.7.8.25-RXN">triphosphoribosyl-dephospho-CoA synthase</a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7830578">Bott94</a>].
<p>
In the presence of acetate and ATP, cell extracts from a <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=G-14821">citC</a>-expressing <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-562"><i>Escherichia coli</i></a> strain were able to reactivate purified citrate lyase from <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-573"><i>Klebsiella pneumoniae</i></a> that had been inactivated by chemical deacetylation of the prosthetic group, suggesting the gene encodes a <a href="/gene?orgid=META&id=MONOMER-17001">[citrate [pro-3S]-lyase] ligase</a>, as enzyme that activates the <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=DEACETYL-CITRATE-LYASE">thiol form of citrate lyase</a> by attaching an <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ACET">acetate</a> to its <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=2-5-PHOSPHORIBOSYL-3-DEPHOSPHO-COA" title="<a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=2-5-PHOSPHORIBOSYL-3-DEPHOSPHO-COA''>2'-(5''-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA</a> is a cofactor of the enzymes <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=ACECITLY-CPLX''>citrate lyase</a> and <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CPLX-7660''>malonate decarboxylase complex</a>. The cofactor is attached via phosphodiester linkage to a serine residue of an acyl-carrier protein subunit of the enzyme complex.&#10;&#10;For biosynthesis of this cofactor, see <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=P2-PWY''>citrate lyase activation</a> and <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=PWY-5796''>malonate decarboxylase activation</a>.">2'-(5''-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA</a> cofactor [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7830578">Bott94</a>].</comment>

<comment datatype="string">This enzyme has been partially purified from <i>Klebsiella aerogenes</i>. It activates an inactive form
of citrate lyase (EC 4.1.3.6) by acetylating it, using S-acetyl phosphopantetheine as the acetyl group donor.
The rate of acetylation followed Michaelis-Menten kinetics with respect to the concentrations of the two
substrates. The maximum rate <i>in vitro</i> occured at 1.6 mM S-acetyl phosphopantetheine and 
1.8 &mu;M of deacetyl citrate lyase [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/4741546">Singh73</a>].</comment>

<comment datatype="string">Citrate lyase deacetylase was purified  from cell extracts of <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ORGANISM&object=TAX-28068"><i>Rubrivivax gelatinosus</i></a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/356">Giffhorn75</a>, <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7460909">Giffhorn80</a>].
The enzyme catalyzed the conversion of <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CITRATE-LYASE">an acetyl-<i>holo</i> [citrate lyase acyl-carrier protein]</a> into
<a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=DEACETYL-CITRATE-LYASE">a [citrate-lyase]</a> and <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ACET">acetate</a> [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7460909">Giffhorn80</a>].
Thioesters such as acetyl-S coenzyme A, acetoacetyl-S coenzyme A, and N-acetyl-S-acetyl-cysteamine
were not hydrolyzed by the enzyme [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/356">Giffhorn75</a>].
<p>
The deacetylase appears to bind to the large subunit of the citrate lyase complex [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/6167565">Giffhorn81</a>].
<p>
The enzyme was strongly inhibited by L-glutamate. The mode of inhibition appeared to be of the linear
mixed type [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/7460909">Giffhorn80</a>].</comment>

<comment datatype="string">Citrate lyase, an anaerobic enzyme, catalyzes the cleavage of citrate to acetate and oxaloacetate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/6354265">Nilekani83</a>]. The citrate molecule is very stable, and needs to be activated prior to cleavage by forming a thioester bond with the enzyme.
<p>
The enzyme is a complex of three subunits (in a 6:6:6 configuration), one of them a dedicated acyl carrier protein (acp).
It is synthesized in an apo form, and is converted to its holo form by the covalent binding of the unusual prosthetic group <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=2-5-PHOSPHORIBOSYL-3-DEPHOSPHO-COA" title="<a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=2-5-PHOSPHORIBOSYL-3-DEPHOSPHO-COA''>2'-(5''-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA</a> is a cofactor of the enzymes <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=ACECITLY-CPLX''>citrate lyase</a> and <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CPLX-7660''>malonate decarboxylase complex</a>. The cofactor is attached via phosphodiester linkage to a serine residue of an acyl-carrier protein subunit of the enzyme complex.&#10;&#10;For biosynthesis of this cofactor, see <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=P2-PWY''>citrate lyase activation</a> and <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=PWY-5796''>malonate decarboxylase activation</a>.">2'-(5''-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA</a> to the [acp] component, resulting in <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=DEACETYL-CITRATE-LYASE">a [citrate-lyase]</a>. However, this holo form is still not fully active - in order to be active, the prosthetic group needs to be acetylated, a reaction catalyzed by the <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=G6344">citC</a>-encoded <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=CITC-MONOMER">citrate lyase synthetase</a>, which generates <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CITRATE-LYASE">an acetyl-<i>holo</i> [citrate lyase acyl-carrier protein]</a>.</comment>

However, this holo form is still not fully active - in order to be active, the prosthetic group needs to be acetylated, a reaction catalyzed by the <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=G6344">citC</a>-encoded <a href="http://biocyc.org/ECOLI/new-image?object=CITC-MONOMER">citrate lyase synthetase</a>, which generates <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CITRATE-LYASE">an acetyl-<i>holo</i> [citrate lyase acyl-carrier protein]</a>.</comment>

<comment datatype="string">Citrate lyase, an anaerobic enzyme, catalyzes the cleavage of citrate to acetate and oxaloacetate [<a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/6354265">Nilekani83</a>]. The citrate molecule is very stable, and needs to be activated prior to cleavage by forming a thioester bond with the enzyme.
<p>
The enzyme is a complex of three subunits (in a 6:6:6 configuration), one of them a dedicated acyl carrier protein (acp).
It is synthesized in an <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=APO-CITRATE-LYASE">apo form</a>, and is converted to its holo form by the covalent binding of the unusual prosthetic group <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=2-5-PHOSPHORIBOSYL-3-DEPHOSPHO-COA" title="<a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?object=2-5-PHOSPHORIBOSYL-3-DEPHOSPHO-COA''>2'-(5''-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA</a> is a cofactor of the enzymes <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=ACECITLY-CPLX''>citrate lyase</a> and <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CPLX-7660''>malonate decarboxylase complex</a>. The cofactor is attached via phosphodiester linkage to a serine residue of an acyl-carrier protein subunit of the enzyme complex.&#10;&#10;For biosynthesis of this cofactor, see <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=P2-PWY''>citrate lyase activation</a> and <a href=''/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=PATHWAY&object=PWY-5796''>malonate decarboxylase activation</a>.">2'-(5''-phosphoribosyl)-3'-dephospho-CoA</a> to the [acp] component, resulting in <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=HOLO-CITRATE-LYASE">a <i>holo</i> [citrate lyase acyl-carrier protein]</a>. However, this holo form is still not fully active - in order to be active, the prosthetic group needs to be acetylated, a reaction catalyzed by <a href="NEW-IMAGE?type=EC-NUMBER&object=EC-6.2.1.22">EC 6.2.1.22, [citrate (<em>pro</em>-3<em>S</em>)-lyase] ligase</a>, resulting in <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CITRATE-LYASE">an acetyl-<i>holo</i> [citrate lyase acyl-carrier protein]</a>.
<p>
The &alpha; subunit of the <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=ACECITLY-CPLX">citrate lyase</a> is a citrate-[acp] transferase that catalyzes the exchange of the bound acetyl group with a citrate molecule, generating <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=Citrate-Lyase-Citryl-Form">a citryl-<i>holo</i> [citrate lyase acyl-carrier protein]</a> and releasing an <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=ACET">acetate</a> molecule.
The &beta; subunit, which is a citryl-[acp] lyase, catalyzes the subsequent step, cleaving the bound citryl group, releasing <a href="/compound?orgid=META&id=OXALACETIC_ACID">oxaloacetate</a> and regenerating <a href="/META/NEW-IMAGE?type=ENZYME&object=CITRATE-LYASE">an acetyl-<i>holo</i> [citrate lyase acyl-carrier protein]</a>. Since the active form is regenrated, the enzyme can continuously catalyze the cleavage reaction.</comment>
